---
title: "How the pool is scored"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(ouanalytics)
library(dplyr)
```

Each player picks OVER or UNDER for every team's preseason win total and puts a
wage on each pick. A team is OVER when its winning percentage is above the line,
UNDER when it is below, and PUSH when the two are equal. A right pick earns its
wage, a wrong pick loses it, and a push earns nothing.

This guide walks the small example pool that ships with the package: three teams,
two players, and two days of games.

```{r inputs}
pool_example$picks
```

## 1. Game results

`compute_game_results()` turns the saved games into one row per team game, with
a running record.

```{r results}
gr <- compute_game_results(pool_example$game_results_raw)
gr %>% select(`Team Name`, `Game Date`, current_wins, current_losses, current_win_perc)
```

## 2. Status against the line

`add_over_under()` compares each game's winning percentage with the team's line.
Alpha is OVER after its first game (100 percent against 50), then PUSH after its
second (50 against 50).

```{r status}
sched <- add_game_scores(gr, tidy_scores(pool_example$scores))
ou <- add_over_under(sched, pool_example$projections, as.Date("2026-10-21"))
ou %>% select(`Team Name`, `Game Date`, `Current Win %`, over_under, flipped)
```

## 3. One row per team per day

`build_standings_grid()` fills in the days a team does not play. A team keeps its
last status on an off day. Before a team's first game it has no status and a
record of 0-0: the Clippers on October 20 below.

```{r grid}
grid <- build_standings_grid(ou, as.Date("2026-10-20"), as.Date("2026-10-21"))
grid %>% select(team, date, `Current Record`, over_under)
```

## 4. Points

`score_picks()` gives each player's points for each team they picked. Points
are missing until the team's first game.

```{r points}
scored <- score_picks(grid, pool_example$picks)
scored %>% select(Date, Player, Team, `Over/Under Pick`, `Current Over/Under`, current_projected_points)
```

## 5. Changes since yesterday

`add_changes()` lists the picks whose points moved. A missing value counts as
0, so a team's first game appears as a change. (Before October 22, 2026 it did
not, and the page said that no scores had changed on days when many had.)

```{r changes}
changes <- add_changes(scored)
rows_for_day(changes, as.Date("2026-10-21"))
```

## 6. Totals and ranking

```{r totals}
ps <- projected_score_by_player(scored)
ps
rank_players(ps, today = as.Date("2026-10-22"))
```

## 7. Everything in one call

`compute_pool()` runs all of the steps above, plus the wins-needed columns, in
the same order the page build uses.

```{r pool}
pool <- with(pool_example, compute_pool(
  game_results_raw, scores, projections, picks, standings,
  params$yesterday, params$today, params$season_start, params$num_games
))
names(pool)
```
